chapter: Back in Houston, Club Ebony and Boo Pleasant
title: The twenty-five-cent Blue Monday sessions
summary: Cobb describes starting Blue Monday afternoons at 25 cents a head, filling the club with off-day workers and visiting jammers and raising the register.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How many pieces did you have in there?

Seven pieces like I had because my book called for seven pieces. And I started a blue Monday there, 25 cents, starting at 2:30 in the evening until -- and you catch beauticians, barbers off on Monday. They go to the -- others go to the -- waiters, waitresses, they off, they go to the golf course and play. The weather is beautiful, and they got nowhere to go, and they come from the golf course.

Liquor store's across the street. And I'm playing the band on the door. Front door register, 25 cents. Seven pieces -- we take the money. We're making $35, $37.00 a day on Mondays from a quarter. My bag raised six or $700.00 on Monday, where before we wasn't doing nothing because they were closed up.
And you got a turnover, some leave, some come in, some leave, some come in. The register's still ringing.
Maybe until 11:00 o'clock that night. Who knows?
On Mondays. Well, we start at 2:30. Well, you got guys come in for a jam.
We wasn't on the stand all the time. They come in. They'd take over and play.
